rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so the ceiling can be raised on cheap, low-risk transforms while keeping cost-heavy ones throttled for this FP-loop-dominated workload: SUB, SPLIT, IBR, and IGV get high Security/Diversity weights plus high cost-dimension weights so they are applied broadly and even to warm functions, since they carry minimal runtime/size/correctness exposure; FLA and BCF retain strong SecurityGain but their RuntimeCost weights are kept low so they are steered away from the hot FFT/float-loop bodies (fourn, main, flops*) where flattening and bogus-flow would compound per-iteration dispatch overhead; ICALL sits in the middle, with a modest CorrectnessRisk weight to limit its reach into the FP-heavy code where indirect-call rewriting offers less cover per unit of call overhead. This trades away obfuscation on the hottest loops (where BCF/FLA add the most slowdown) in exchange for maximizing structural diversity everywhere else, preserving the round-0 correctness result while increasing reverse-engineering resistance on non-loop-critical code.
